plants.name: Prunus × yedoensis
plants.description: A graceful deciduous tree covered in clouds of pale pink to white five-petaled blossoms that appear before the leaves emerge. It is the most widely planted ornamental cherry in Japan and a centerpiece of spring celebrations in temperate parks worldwide.
plants.bloomingSeason: Late March to mid-April in temperate Northern Hemisphere
plants.location: Japan, Washington D.C. (USA), Korea, and temperate regions of Europe and North America
plants.funFact: The famous cherry trees around the Tidal Basin in Washington D.C. were a gift from Tokyo in 1912, and their peak bloom date is closely tracked each year by the National Park Service.

plants.name: Narcissus pseudonarcissus
plants.description: A hardy bulbous perennial with trumpet-shaped yellow flowers surrounded by paler yellow petals. It grows in woodlands, meadows, and hedgerows, and has given rise to countless garden cultivars.
plants.bloomingSeason: March to April in temperate Northern Hemisphere
plants.location: Western Europe, especially the United Kingdom, France, and Spain; naturalized in North America
plants.funFact: All parts of the daffodil contain the alkaloid lycorine, and compounds from related Narcissus species such as galantamine are used in medicines for Alzheimer's disease.

plants.name: Cercis canadensis
plants.description: A small deciduous tree whose bare branches and even trunk burst with clusters of magenta-pink pea-like flowers before the heart-shaped leaves appear. It is a favorite of early-season pollinators and a staple of woodland edges and gardens.
plants.location: Eastern and central North America, from southern Ontario to Mexico
plants.funFact: Redbud flowers are edible and have a mildly tart flavor; they are sometimes added to salads, and the trees display cauliflory, meaning flowers grow directly from the trunk.
